name: ProPresenter
tagline: Live presentation software for churches and events: song lyrics, media, multi-screen output, stage displays.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The thing most people actually use ProPresenter for, pushing song lyrics and background images to a projector while watching a preview on your laptop, is a genuinely small program. An agent can build that in an evening with Electron: a library of text files, playlists, a second-display output window, arrow keys, fade to black. What it cannot build in one sitting is the live production layer: alpha-channel video playback that never stutters, stage displays with timers and notes, NDI and Blackmagic capture, MIDI and remote control, SongSelect import, Bible lookup, and the general property of not dying at 10:45am on a Sunday. If you are one person running slides for a small room, the DIY version is fine. If you are running a service with a video team, it is not.
coreLoopDIY: A desktop app that holds a library of slide decks and song lyrics as plain text, shows an operator view with current and next slide, and mirrors the live slide full screen onto a second display with background media and fade transitions.
requirements: Node and a desktop machine with a second display or projector output
Local folder of background images and videos
No accounts, no cloud, no network connection needed
whatYouLose: Rock-solid live media playback: hardware-accelerated video, alpha channel masks, looping backgrounds that do not hitch mid-transition
Stage display outputs with next-slide, clocks, countdowns and operator notes
Broadcast plumbing: NDI, Syphon, capture cards, multi-screen edge cases, resolution mismatches
CCLI SongSelect and Bible library import, so every song becomes a copy-paste job
Macros, MIDI and remote triggering, plus the muscle memory of a volunteer team that already knows the real thing
moatNotes: The moat is not features on a list, it is twenty years of edge cases in live video output on machines nobody controls.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the failure mode is public. A slide app that crashes in your bedroom is a bug; one that crashes in front of four hundred people is a story people tell. ProPresenter is bought by volunteers and part-time tech directors who need something a new person can learn in an hour and that handles whatever projector, capture card and 4K MP4 shows up. That is support, documentation and a decade of defensive code, none of which comes out of a one-shot prompt.
notes: Fine for a living room or a 30-seat room with one operator. Anything with a video team should keep paying.
prompt:
Build a local-only live slide presenter desktop app called "Lumen". No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry, no analytics.

Stack, non-negotiable: Electron with TypeScript, Vite for the renderer, plain HTML and CSS, no UI framework. Package with electron-builder for macOS and Windows. All state on disk, no database server.

Data model: a library folder chosen by the user, default ~/Lumen. Inside it, decks/ holds one .md file per song or deck. Slides are separated by a line containing only "---". The first line of the file is the title. Optional YAML front matter may set a background file and text alignment. media/ holds background images and videos. playlists/ holds .json files that are ordered lists of deck filenames. Parse on startup, watch the folder with chokidar and hot-reload on change.

Windows:
1. Operator window. Left: playlist and deck list. Center: grid of slide thumbnails for the selected deck, current slide outlined. Right: live preview and next-slide preview.
2. Output window. Frameless, full screen on a display the user picks from a dropdown of all detected displays. Renders only the live slide. Nothing else, ever.
3. Stage window, optional, on a third display. Shows current slide text large, next slide smaller, and a wall clock.

Behavior: arrow keys and space advance and reverse through slides, continuing into the next deck in the playlist. B fades the output to black, L shows a logo image, Escape clears. Slide changes cross-fade over a configurable duration, default 300ms. Text renders centered with a configurable font size, a thin drop shadow, and auto-shrink so long verses fit without overflow. Backgrounds can be an image or a looping muted video rendered behind the text.

Include a deck editor: edit the raw markdown in a textarea, save to disk, thumbnails refresh. Include a settings panel for library path, output display, logo image, font, and transition duration, persisted to a JSON config in app data.

Explicitly out of scope, do not attempt: NDI, Syphon, capture cards, MIDI, network remote control, CCLI SongSelect, Bible lookup, multi-camera, edge blending, cloud sync.

Ship a README covering the folder layout, the keyboard shortcuts, and how to run in dev and build a packaged app. Seed the library with two example decks and a placeholder background so it does something useful on first launch.
